extracted.intended_audience: government officials and policymakers in developing countries seeking MCC partnership; development practitioners and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Millennium Challenge Corporation's standards for selecting partner countries, required country commitments, grant types, implementation expectations, priority sectors, and intended outcomes for MCC-funded activities. Useful for governments and practitioners preparing proposals or assessing fit for MCC programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to just and democratic governance, economic freedom and investing in their populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries must be 'committed to just and democratic governance, economic freedom and investing in their populations.' MCC partners with the world’s poorest countries that demonstrate these commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commitment is foundational to eligibility and partnership; MCC emphasizes that investing in well-governed countries is the most effective use of development dollars and incentivizes reform even before selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection based on 20 independent and transparent policy indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC’s Board examines a country’s performance on 20 independent and transparent policy indicators and selects countries based on policy performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is competitive and indicator-driven; countries are assessed objectively across these indicators (the page references the 20 indicators without enumerating them). Strong performance on these indicators is necessary for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-led solutions (proposal development and priority setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected countries are required to identify their priorities for achieving sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction and develop their MCC proposals in broad consultation within their society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCC expects country ownership of program design; proposals should reflect broad domestic consultation and clearly articulated national priorities that MCC then helps refine in partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-led implementation with a local accountable entity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a country is awarded an MCC compact, it sets up a local accountable entity to manage and oversee all aspects of implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation responsibility lies with a country-established entity; fund monitoring is expected to be rigorous, transparent, and often managed through independent fiscal agents to ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on results and evidence-based impact evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC is committed to producing results and ensuring that the American people are getting a good return on their investment, employing technically rigorous, systematic and transparent methods of projecting, tracking and evaluating the impacts of its programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should include measurable results and be designed with rigorous M&E (monitoring and evaluation) plans; transparency in projections and tracking is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limited grants promoting economic growth, reducing poverty, and strengthening institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC provides time-limited grants promoting economic growth, reducing poverty, and strengthening institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are not open-ended; they are designed as time-bound investments targeting economic growth, poverty reduction, and institutional strengthening rather than indefinite aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effective, transparent programming with a lean administrative approach
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC emphasizes cost-effective and transparent projects, a lean staff, and an evidence-based approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should demonstrate cost-effectiveness and transparency; MCC’s own operating model values lean administration and evidence-based decision-making as part of partner selection and program execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity with other U.S. and international development programs and enabling private investment
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC grants are designed to complement other U.S. and international development programs, as well as create an enabling environment for private sector investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project design should avoid duplication, align with broader development efforts, and facilitate private sector engagement and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact: large, five-year grants for selected countries meeting eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Compacts are large, five-year grants for selected countries that meet MCC’s eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compacts are the main instrument for countries that pass MCC’s selection; they are sizable and multi-year and require demonstrated policy performance and capacity for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Compacts for Regional Investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent Compacts are grants that promote cross-border economic integration, and increase regional trade and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grants target regional projects requiring multi-country cooperation and aim to advance integration and trade beyond a single-country compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold Programs for countries close to passing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold Programs are smaller grants focused on policy and institutional reform in selected countries that come close to passing MCC’s eligibility criteria and show a firm commitment to improving their policy performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold Programs are intended as capacity-building or policy-reform support to help countries improve indicator performance and become eligible for larger compacts in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority sectors and project areas eligible for MCC investment
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC supports country-led projects in areas like: agriculture and irrigation; anti-corruption; education; energy and power (generation, distribution, and transmission); finance and enterprise development; health; land rights and access to land; transportation infrastructure (roads, bridges, ports); water supply and sanitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with these sectoral priorities and demonstrate how interventions in these areas will contribute to economic growth, poverty reduction, and institutional strengthening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and financial oversight via independent fiscal agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring of funds is rigorous, transparent and often managed through independent fiscal agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial oversight mechanisms and independent fiscal management are expected components of program implementation to ensure proper use of grant funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended impacts and success outcomes for MCC investments
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC investments aim to: create jobs and expand markets; build a more stable world; promote growth through infrastructure; invest in the next generation; incentivize policy and institutional reform; empower women and girls; increase the capacity of partner governments; give entrepreneurs tools to succeed; lay the groundwork for healthy communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project design and evaluation should link activities to these intended outcomes and articulate credible pathways and metrics for achieving and measuring these impacts.
